title: Bounded aggregate result-home forwarding prototype, 2026-10-21
status: Retired from the shipping optimizer registry and production library on 2026-10-21 after zero changed inputs across all 44 current Lua, QuickJS and SQLite translation units. The standalone implementation, proof tests, native integration test and probe remain for research. Historical pre-priority counts below are not current activation evidence. See experiment-reconciliation-20261021.html.
implementation: crates/keel-opt/src/aggregate_return.rs: run(&mut Module) -> usize (eliminated complete copies). The aggregate-return pass wraps this entry point; the standalone probe reports copy counts for retained IR evidence.
transform: Change only the selected direct call sret argument to a newly materialized StackAddr for the existing independent destination. Remove the exact copy loads and stores. Preserve the callee, its signature, all other call arguments and evaluation order. DCE can remove now-unused address computations; this prototype does not change frame layout or allocation.
proof: Callee is a defined local symbol, with an exactly matching call signature: no exported/interposable/declaration-only body assumptions. Single block, no variadic/returns-twice/scalar returns, 1..64-byte leading sret.

Every result byte is written exactly once. All stores use nonvolatile sret-derived in-bounds constant-offset addresses. No load, call, intrinsic, inline assembly, trap, exception, address-to-integer conversion, other-address store, or sret-address observation is admitted. Other computations are explicitly whitelisted nontrapping scalar operations. This proves no capture and no observation; it does not infer nocapture from ordinarycall or small-register ABI.

Source home is an exact-sized fixed slot. Whole-function operand closure admits only the selected call (sret argument once, no overlapping byval/source argument), bounded constant address derivation and the eliminated exact copy loads. Extra reads, writes, scalar observations, aliases through unknown operations, capture, indirect calls and cross-block copies reject.

Destination is a distinct exact-sized fixed slot with alignment at least the source and result-layout alignment. Each constructor store must also be aligned by the destination declaration at its exact byte offset; checking only a maximum base alignment is insufficient. Its own address closure permits bounded ordinary loads/stores/address derivation. Any calls receiving destination-derived addresses must follow the completed copy in the same block. Such calls may capture: this remains safe because the proven constructor has no loads, calls or observers through which to see that capture, and the destination identity is unchanged.

Between call and completed copy, at most 128 instructions: only constants, recognized stack/constant addresses, selected source loads and matching destination stores. Every byte copied once at identical offsets; every load result used solely by the eliminated copy. Moving writes across this interval cannot expose another observer or trap: both homes are valid fixed objects, the constructor is nontrapping and has no external effect, and no intervening effect is admitted.

Whole-function rejection of every intrinsic (including FrameAddress and stack lifetime operations), inline assembly, invoke and direct/indirect returns-twice calls. Whole-module file/type debug metadata and all function debug homes reject. No narrowing of existing stack-forward escape rules.

Hard budgets: 128 callee instructions, 512 callee values, 64 result bytes; 50000 caller instructions, 100000 caller values; 2000000 charged instruction+operand units for repeated closure scans; at most 128 matching instructions per candidate. One address walk, no fixpoint, recursive proof, call graph traversal, or CFG search. Budget exhaustion preserves valid partial progress.

validation.native: Clang-built reference and transformed direct/assembly-text object routes executed across x=-100..100; includes 16-byte register results, 24-byte memory results, explicit byval snapshots and capture-after-copy.
validation.cross_target: ARM Mach-O and x86-64 Linux ELF direct/assembly-text .text matches. x86-64 objects not executed.
validation.logs: target/aggregate-return-20261021/report.json and report.html; complete serialization metadata in lock.jsonl

examples.exact_IR: JS_NewInt32 result ss5 copied to args[0] ss2, then args passed to js_typed_array_create.
JS_NewBool result ss1 copied to func_data[0] ss0, then passed to JS_NewCFunctionData.

limitations: No return-slot/parameter/heap forwarding; no generic escaped-slot admission or exported ABI change. No target ABI inference is needed.
No JS_CallInternal transformation in either supplied retained module. This does not resolve hot-interpreter homes; parent backend address-save elision is complementary.
No speed, actual frame-size or performance attribution claim. Static removal: Full 12 loads + 12 stores; guarded 8 loads + 8 stores. No performance commands run.

alignment_review_response.change: Track every constructor store offset and alignment promise; reject destinations whose declared base alignment or byte-offset residue cannot establish every promise. Preserve result-layout alignment too.
alignment_review_response.coverage: 24-byte offset-8/align-16 reproducer rejects unchanged; stronger-than-declaration base promise rejects; valid offset/base alignment cases still forward.
